messages:
mike (support): FYI customer acme-prod is reporting intermittent 504s and request timeouts on the hosted inference API (/v1/generate). Happens during tenant burst traffic. Gateway logs show backend 5xx / "scaleup timeout waiting for model-ready" messages. Tagging @dana and @sara for triage.


dana (support-lead): What time window? any repro steps from the customer? can they reproduce with a small load test? @ben it might be an infra scaling thing.


mike (support): Started around 2026-03-16T21:10Z and recurred during a second traffic spike ~21:18Z. Customer provided this quick repro (they run this from a CI runner):

```
# concurrent 20 clients for 30s
for i in {1..20}; do curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": "hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

They see ~10-15% 504/timeout responses on first burst. Subsequent requests succeed once pods are ready.


ben (platform): Pasted a small snippet from the gateway logs around the spike: 

```
2026-03-16T21:18:04Z gateway svc=api route=/v1/generate status=504 err="backend timeout"
2026-03-16T21:18:05Z backendmgr tenant=acme-prod msg="scaleup: waiting for pods (0->2)" deadline=2026-03-16T21:19:05Z
2026-03-16T21:19:10Z backendmgr tenant=acme-prod msg="pod started but readiness=false model-init=45.3s"
2026-03-16T21:19:40Z backendmgr tenant=acme-prod msg="pod ready, routing traffic"
```


oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-1884. Oncall: @sara (eng-runtime). Priority: P2.


sara (eng-runtime): Quick notes from k8s/keda/HPA view: KEDA ScaledObject pollInterval=30s, cooldownPeriod=300s. HPA configured targetCPU=60%. Model binary download + quant init measured ~40-50s for this model on our current instance/quantization. Readiness probe currently 10s. Gateway backend timeout was 30s.

So the chain is: KEDA observes metric -> scale event -> K8s schedules pods -> pod starts + model init (~45s) -> readiness fails until model loaded -> gateway times out at 30s -> client sees 504. There's both a timing mismatch (gateway < model-init) and scaler reaction granularity (poll interval + cooldown) making the first requests suffer.


liz (customer-success): Also saw a blip earlier where our auth connector returned 401s during a token rotation window; those 401s caused a handful of scaler webhook calls to fail briefly. Not sure if that made the scaler slow to react for one of the bursts.


ben (platform): Immediate mitigations I applied: bumped the tenant's Deployment minReplicas to 2, increased pod readiness probe timeout to 120s (grace for model init), and increased gateway backend timeout to 90s for acme-prod routing. Changes applied at 21:30Z. Monitoring now.


mike (support): Customer reports errors dropped to ~0.5% after the fixes during the next burst. Good short-term result. :thumbsup:


sara (eng-runtime): Long-term remediation suggestions:
- add a model prewarm lifecycle hook so new pods run a lightweight model load on start (or keep a warm worker in a pool)
- change scaler metrics: have KEDA/HPA consider queue length or in-flight requests (steady fast signal) instead of only CPU to catch bursty traffic faster
- reduce scaler pollInterval to 5-10s for critical tenants and tune cooldowns
- provide a fast-fallback model variant that inits <5s for cold-starts (lower quality but avoids 504)
- audit token rotation path so scaler auth/webhook calls never fail during rotation (liz please share rotation window)


liz (customer-success): I'll attach the customer's rotation schedule in the follow-up ticket and confirm they can avoid rotation during high-traffic jobs.


dana (support-lead): Assigning follow-ups: eng-runtime (sara) to spec prewarm + fallback variant; platform (ben) to evaluate KEDA poll/cooldown defaults and per-tenant scaling overrides; CS (liz) to coordinate auth rotation windows with customer. Ben/Sara please create tickets with repro, perf numbers, and rollout plan. :white_check_mark:


ben (platform): Will open KF ticket KF-4721 with infra repro steps + config diffs. I'll include the exact k8s events, HPA/KEDA snapshots, and the commands we used to reproduce.


mike (support): Thanks everyone — closing the incident channel after follow-ups are filed. Will update customer with mitigation summary and ETA for medium-term fixes.


sara (eng-runtime): One extra note: we should also consider increasing gauge in gateway for backend timeout for model-initializing endpoints only, rather than blanket increase, so we don't accidentally expose other slow upstreams. I'll include that in the KF-4721 spec.


dana (support-lead): Acknowledged. Postmortem + action items due EOD+2. :rotating_light:
